newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy stocks surge after oil price jump.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy stocks surge after oil price jump.

text.p: Investors pushed up the value of Canadian energy sector stocks in a flurry of activity Tuesday, the first day of trading in Canada after a big jump in oil prices.
The Toronto Stock Exchange Oil and Gas Index surged 48.19 points to 5,825.04 by midday Tuesday, as trading resumed after Canada's Thanksgiving Day holiday on Monday.
The surge followed Monday's surprise US$0.96 leap in the NYMEX November crude contract, which closed at US$25.62 a barrel. The price was just shy of the US$25.70 post-Gulf War high set last spring.
The oil price jump was attributed to news of renewed violence in Iraq's northern Kurdish regions and persistently low heating oil stocks in Western markets.
The renewed Iraqi tensions were said to have reminded crude markets of the missing oil supplies previously expected under a United Nations oil-for-food exchange with Iraq.
The NYMEX November contract was down C$0.34 on Tuesday to US$25.30 per barrel.
Top Canadian energy actives included Stampeder Exploration Ltd, up 0.30 to 6.10, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, ahead 0.35 to 24.05, and Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, unchanged at 8.90.
Market watchers said Stampeder's activity resulted from arbitragers settling accounts after the company's C$512 million takeover of Morgan Hydrocarbons.
But several other companies rode the crest of the seller's oil market.
"People are after anything that has oil leverage," said Martin Molyneaux, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp.
"Yesterday, we had a ton of messages on our phone from U.S. people wondering why we weren't working."
The oil-price enthusiasm only served to add to the sector's recent attraction to large investors because of its relative financial health and projections for strong production increases, he said.
Other big gainers on Tuesday included Canadian Natural Resources, which expects its oil output to soar in 1997, as well as PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, Talisman Energy Inc and Renaissance Energy Ltd.
Shares of Renaissance, the busiest driller in western Canada, were up C$1 to C$42.50 on volume of 114,248.
